sentences.text: Record of the Court below is received.
The appeal being arguable is admitted for final hearing.
Heard on I.A.No.1850/2024, which is an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant No.2 Ambikesh Tripathi.

The appellant No.2 has been convicted for the offences punishable under Section 302/34, 498A of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. life, RI for life, RI for 3 years, RI for 1 year respectively with fine of Rs.25,000/-, Rs.2,000/-, Rs.1,000/- respectively with default stipulation.
The earlier application was dismissed on merit vide order dated 04/10/2023.

Considering the Dying Declaration and Marg Intimation which shows direct nexus of the present appellant No.2 who is brother-in-law (Jeth) of the deceased with the offence in question and after dismissal of previous application on merit for suspension sentence by this Court vide order dated 04.10.2023, learned counsel is unable to point out any change in circumstances.

Thus, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and as to the fact that the earlier application for suspension of sentence was 2 CRA-1018-2022 dismissed on merit by this Court vide order dated 04.10.2023, and since then there is no change in circumstances, this Court is not inclined to suspend the substantive jail sentence of the appellant No.2.
Accordingly, IA No.1850/2024 stands dismissed.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) (AVANINDRA KUM  JUDGE JUDGE  Astha Smt Neelu @ Neelam Tripathi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75459526/
